newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to raise cost of employing foreign workers.
newsitem.headline: Israel to raise cost of employing foreign workers.

text.p: The cost of employing a foreign worker in Israel will go up by 5,532 shekels a year if a package of recommendations on tax and other benefits is adopted, Israel's Treasury said on Sunday.
Under the proposals formulated by a Treasury committee, employers will have to pay 300 shekels for a permit to employ a foreign worker and a 3,000 shekel annual fee once the permit is granted.

In addition, employers would be required to help contribute 700 shekels a month per worker to a social security fund for foreign workers. The money would be paid the worker so long as he leaves Israel before his permit expires, the Treasury said.
The committee also recommended eliminating various tax benefits for foreign workers.

"These special benefits are one of the reasons that the cost of employing foreign workers is less than employing local workers and this goes against the government's policy of minimizing the number of foreign workers in Israel," the Treasury said in a statement.
The proposals would also raise an estimated 100 million shekels in income for the government, which would be used to help close the budget deficit.

The government estimates that as of August 1 there were 87,000 legal foreign workers in Israel. Many of them are replacing Palestinians from the occupied West Bank and Gaza who have not been able to enter the country because of repeated border closures.
The recommendations assume the number will fall to 70,000 if the proposals are implemented.
The recommendations will be presented to Labour and Social Affairs Minister Eli Yishai.
